localPublicDevcontainer.hostSurface: Windows-hosted checkout with Docker Desktop Linux engine
notes: The earlier WSL-path failure was a machine-surface mismatch between the broken Linux Docker CLI and Windows docker.exe path translation, not a repo build failure.
The repo-owned blocker was .devcontainer/devcontainer.json forcing overrideCommand=false against the base Node image, which caused the container to exit before postCreateCommand completed.
After setting overrideCommand=true, the public devcontainer completed npm ci, npm run compile, and npm run test:design-contract successfully on this machine.
The hosted proof runs against the curated public GitHub source repo rather than the authority repo.
The governed Linux host bootstrap now installs both VS Code runtime libraries and the xauth/Xvfb support needed by xvfb-run on Debian-hosted Codespaces surfaces.

The retained hosted smoke now proves Docker Linux image cold pull plus containerized CreateComparisonReport reachability on the public product surface; semantic compare acceptance on the canonical fixture remains Gate D human judgment.
This is the governed canonical Gate D human pass on the public Docker-only product.
The retained preflight packet and the retained review submission now close the public-acceptance blocker for the exact v1.0.0 line.

rationale: Public testers need a low-friction sample repository inside devcontainer and Codespaces sessions.
Cloning ni/labview-icon-editor on every startup would add network cost and side effects to every public development session.
An opt-in governed helper keeps the tester path easy without making a third-party clone a mandatory startup dependency.
